A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Memora research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Memora benchmark results, component ablations, retrieval latency measurements and GRPO experiments, alongside some explicitly borrowed baseline scores.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds construction-cost, construction-model, component and memory-update results, including Appendix F.

M1.justification: v2 introduces an optional construction optimization that predicts offsets into source material instead of generating full memory values (Section 5.2.4, Table 6). The core abstraction/cue architecture, consolidation equations, retrieval actions and policy-training objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same LoCoMo conversational tasks and LongMemEval S coverage. The added analyses vary construction models, components and update settings within existing coverage; they introduce no new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds HippoRAG to the LoCoMo comparison, reporting an overall judge score of 0.471. Existing benchmark comparators remain, and the new construction-cost comparison also evaluates Mem0 alongside standard and offset-based Memora.

E3.justification: The reported GRPO configuration changes from Qwen-2.5-3B-Instruct with a 10/10/80 train/dev/test split to Qwen-2.5-1.5B with a 70/30 train/test split. Added protocols compare construction models and offset generation, test update thresholds with cues and episodic memory disabled, and group construction events by accumulated memory count. These substantially expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds component build-up ablations, construction-cost and offset-optimization analysis, and robustness to a smaller construction model (Tables 3, 6 and 7). New Appendix F tests threshold sensitivity and update behavior as memory accumulates (Tables 17–18). The earlier retrieval/granularity ablations and three case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both specify seed 42 and retain the same point-estimate and latency-percentile reporting practices. Neither adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. New average timings and update ratios are additional results.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include abstraction-only scores of 0.795/0.801, standard/offset construction times of 1322.0/739.9 seconds, nano-construction scores of 0.763/0.851, and threshold/growth statistics. Figure 2 replaces GRPO/base results of 0.841/0.836 with 0.841/0.829 under the changed model and split; multi-hop changes from a tie to GRPO underperforming its base. These are different-setting results. Retained headline Memora scores remain 0.863 on LoCoMo and 87.4% on LongMemEval.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, policy-update derivations and Appendix D theorems and proofs are unchanged. The former standalone theoretical-analysis summary moves into Section 2. Appendix F supplies empirical discussion, not a new formal scaling proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: harmonic abstraction/cue organization, policy-guided retrieval, RAG/KG special cases and benchmark-superiority claims. The headline performance and token-reduction claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning construction and scalability: comparable construction time supports attribution to representation quality, policy retrieval compensates for weaker construction models, and lower update thresholds cause over-consolidation. It also interprets stable update ratios as evidence of linear consolidation cost without a growing bottleneck (Section 5.2.4 and Appendix F). Existing retrieval/context interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the default update threshold of 0.80 and describes offset-based construction. It replaces a promised future code release with a stated release and repository pointer. Existing extraction prompts, evaluator settings and hardware information in Appendices A–C are retained; repository availability is not independently established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds the HippoRAG citation and a dedicated positioning paragraph contrasting content-based indexing and fixed graph schemas with Memora's separate navigation layer. This expands the explanation of an existing distinction; the remaining cited literature and theoretical positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds positioning and construction-analysis passages, introduces Appendix F, and incorporates the former theoretical-analysis summary into related work. It also updates front matter and makes localized wording edits. Most existing prose, method exposition and appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The experimental displays expand substantially through new component, construction-cost, construction-model, threshold and memory-growth tables (Tables 3, 6–7 and 17–18). Table 1 gains a baseline row, and Figure 2 changes its model legend and plotted bars. Existing ablation, latency and case-study tables remain after renumbering; Figure 1 receives a caption edit.

improvement.justification: v1 assessed retrieval latency but lacked construction-cost evaluation and direct primary-abstraction controls. v2 adds evidence addressing these gaps, construction-model and update analyses, and concrete code-access information. These improve practical assessment and empirical support. The gains are limited by absent uncertainty estimates and the unsupported inference from stable update ratios to linear construction cost in Appendix F.
